motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that an ad hoc EHV working group be formed to identify funding solutions and ensure that families and individuals housed can remain housed. The EHV workgroup will include the Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles (HACLA), City Administrative Office (CAO), Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD), and Chief Legislative Analyst (CLA). The working group should focus on the following priorities and report back to City Council within 90 days on: Identifying funding options to seek one-time funding to ensure EHV holders remain housed through the length of the program (2030), including but not limited to Measure A funds, ULA funds, State Proposition 1 funding, and philanthropic funding. Identifying and transitioning eligible EHV holders to Continuum of Care slots and turnover project based voucher slots. • Crafting and implementing an exit strategy for EHV holders. This could include leveraging existing programs to ensure proper case management, job readiness coaching, etc. I FURTHER MOVE that HACLA with assistance from the CAO, LAHD and CLA report back to City Council within 90 days on the feasibility of implementing a local subsidy program that does not rely on federal funding sources to keep individuals housed. This report should include: Validated cost projections to keep EHV households stably housed through 2030; and proposed funding plan Landscape of local and state funders that could either offer funds or provide permanent housing and tenant-based subsidies. PRESENTED BY: ed NITHYA RAMAN Councilmember, 4th District SECONDED BY:

documents.excerpt: Housing Authority of the City of Los Sustaining Angeles Housing for Emergency Housing Informational Briefing: Voucher Recipients Section 8 Funding Update Housing and Homelessness Committee August 5, 2026 Council File (11) 25-0651 August 5, 2026 The Challenge HACLA currently administers federal Emergency Housing Voucher(EHV) funding that supports approximately 2,700 households, which include over 4,300 people. Federal funding for the EHV program was set to expire by December 2026. It would have cost HACLA approximately $57 million to continue rental assistance for these households once funding expired. Without intervention, 4,300 vulnerable renters risked eviction and potential returns to homelessness. 2 HACLA’s Response • HACLA’s Board of Commissioners promptly determined that addressing the needs of EHV households would be a key priority for the agency. • Following the July 1, 2025, City Council motion, HACLA collaborated with local partners to explore and assess alternative funding options. Raised awareness with LACAHSA and the Leadership Table of the regional impact. • LACAHSA granted $500,000 to HR&A to assist HACLA and other housing agencies in L.A. County with developing a transition plan to support impacted households in stabilizing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing services. • HACLA engaged in advocacy efforts across federal, state, and local government levels as well as through national advocacy with U.S. Conference of Mayors. • With assistance from HACLA’s AmeriCorps volunteers, ongoing direct support was provided to EHV households during this time. 3 HACLA’s HCV Shortfall Has Ended • With the funding notices now in hand—and after confirmation with HUD’s Shortfall Team—HACLA is no longer in a funding shortfall for its Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCV). • With the $976 million HACLA received in CY2026 funding for HCV tenant- based renewals, HACLA will be able to transition all EHV households to HCV, thereby keeping families stably housed. • LACDA has also announced that they will be able to transition their EHV households to Housing Choice Vouchers. • Additionally, HACLA will process the approximately 3,000 applications which were paused last year due to funding constraints. That timeline will be announced soon. 4 EHV Recipients Will Be Able to Maintain Current Their Housing • EHV recipients will be absorbed into the HCV program, allowing eligible households to continue receiving housing assistance. Households will transition effective September 1, 2026. • Families will remain in their current units, and property owners will continue to receive support through HACLA communications and ongoing Housing Assistance Payments (HAP). This will be seamless and HACLA will not need anything new from either the tenant or the owner. • Households with delinquent annual recertifications, unresolved inspection issues, or portability-related matters will be addressed separately to ensure a smooth transition. 5 Positive Impact in Every C
